props.title: Mortal Kombat
props.initialSlug: Warriors battle in mystical tournament for Earth's fate

sections.content: **Mortal Kombat** (1995) punched through Hollywood's "video game curse" as one of the first genuinely entertaining game adaptations. Director Paul W.S. Anderson delivered exactly what fans wanted - faithful character designs, authentic martial arts choreography, and that iconic techno theme song. While **Street Fighter** (1994) went campy with Jean-Claude Van Damme, Mortal Kombat embraced its supernatural tournament premise with straight-faced intensity. Christopher Lambert's scenery-chewing Raiden and Cary-Hiroyuki Tagawa's deliciously evil Shang Tsung gave the film personality without descending into pure cheese.

sections.content: The film sparked a brief renaissance of martial arts tournament movies in the mid-90s. **Bloodsport** (1988) had established the template, but Mortal Kombat modernized it with CGI effects and mystical elements that influenced later works like **The Matrix** (1999). The film's success also paved the way for better video game adaptations like **Resident Evil** (2002) and **Silent Hill** (2006), proving games could work as cinema with the right approach to the source material.

What's fascinating about **Mortal Kombat** (1995) is how it managed to adapt an infamously violent game into a PG-13 film without losing its edge. The movie cleverly focused on martial arts spectacle over gore, similar to how **Big Trouble in Little China** (1986) balanced supernatural elements with kung fu action. This approach influenced later adaptations like **DOA: Dead or Alive** (2006) and **Prince of Persia: The Sands of Time** (2010). SUBHEAD: Legacy and Influence

sections.content: The film's impact extends beyond just video game movies. Its blend of practical martial arts and early CGI effects created a template for how to handle supernatural fighting on screen. This influence can be seen in everything from **Blade** (1998) to **The One** (2001). Even modern Marvel movies like **Shang-Chi and the Legend of the Ten Rings** (2021) echo some of Mortal Kombat's approach to mystical martial arts action.
